files.what_it_shows: Rendered page of the overview map above.

searched: The Federal Register notice for 2026-15884, which gave docket CP26-19-000.
FERC eLibrary search of docket CP26-19, about 120 filings listed.
Downloaded the environmental assessment and the company's updated overview map from the April 2026 data response.

The detailed alignment sheets (Exhibit G and the agency supplement) are filed as Critical Energy Infrastructure Information or privileged, so they were not downloadable. Kentucky Public Service Commission was not needed.
notes: The map is a 1:250,000 overview, but the red workspace follows the route closely and has many named towns and roads a georeferencer can match. The workspace includes the lines to be abandoned as well as the new pipe, so the corridor is wider than one pipeline. The northern end is at the Ohio River near Fort Thomas and Cincinnati. The southern end is near Foster and Carntown in Bracken County. The project is mostly in Kentucky, with a short end in Hamilton County, Ohio. The map shows the corridor within a few miles of Alexandria and US Highway 27. The sheet length is 30.2 miles. This straight-line corridor looks about 25 to 30 miles, so it is consistent. The FERC download page is a JavaScript application, so the URL checker could not read it, but the files were downloaded and read directly.
